commits.pr_title: [Core][Refactor] Move KV cache planning logic to kv_cache_planning.py
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Move the KV cache grouping, sizing, and capacity-planning logic from `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py` into a new module, `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_planning.py`. This is a pure code move with no behavior change.

Split out from #53558 so the large move can be reviewed separately from the pluggable `KVCacheConfigBuilder` change.

## Claims

- `kv_cache_utils.py` goes from about 2.8k to about 1.2k lines. It keeps the block, hash, and free-queue utilities, plus the helpers that consume a finished `KVCacheConfig`: `get_max_concurrency_for_kv_cache_config`, `generate_scheduler_kv_cache_config`, `get_kv_cache_capacity`, and `update_kv_cache_capacity`.
- `kv_cache_planning.py` holds the planning path: `get_kv_cache_configs`, `get_kv_cache_groups`, `get_kv_cache_config_from_groups`, page-size unification, packed/hybrid grouping, memory and max-model-len estimation, auto-fit, and TP-replica helpers (38 functions).
- Function names and bodies are unchanged. No compatibility re-exports are left in `kv_cache_utils.py`; all in-tree callers are updated.

## Validation

- Every moved function is byte-identical to `origin/main`. This was checked by comparing each top-level definition with the AST. Reviewers can confirm with:
  ```bash
  git diff --color-moved=dimmed-zebra origin/main...HEAD -- vllm/v1/core/
  ```
- `pre-commit` passes (ruff, mypy, typos, and the test-tethering checks).
- Ran the affected unit tests on CPU, on both this branch and `origin/main`. Both give the same result: **294 passed, 19 skipped**.
  ```bash
  pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \
    tests/v1/core/test_contiguous_kv_packing.py \
    tests/v1/engine/test_init_error_messaging.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_config.py \
    tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_worker.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hidden_states_connector.py \
    tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_kv_cache_layout.py \
    tests/v1/worker/test_dsv4_packed_zeroer_geometry.py
  ```
- `tests/models/test_initialization.py`, `tests/models/test_dspark_mla.py`, and `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py` import and collect cleanly. They need a GPU, so they are left to CI.

## Details

Besides the move itself, these updates keep behavior and CI coverage the same:

- **Imports:** updated in `v1/engine/core.py`, `v1/hisparse/layout.py`, `v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py`, `v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py`, and the affected tests.
- **Monkeypatch targets:** the `get_hisparse_host_pool_bytes` patches and the `max_memory_usage_bytes` patch string now point at `kv_cache_planning`. Patching the old module would silently stop taking effect.
- **Subprocess test:** the import embedded in the script string of `test_is_kv_cache_spec_uniform` now uses the new module.
- **Buildkite:** wherever `.buildkite/test-amd.yaml` and `.buildkite/test_areas/lm_eval.yaml` list `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py` as a source dependency, `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_planning.py` is now listed too. Changes to the moved code still trigger the same jobs.

Out-of-tree code that imports planning functions from `vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_utils` needs to switch to `vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_planning`.

Follow-up: #53558 can rebase on top of this, so its diff only contains the builder changes.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Enable decoder SWA bounded replay
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

#58132 added decoder-side SWA bounded replay for the CUDA model. This PR enables it on ROCm. During eager prefill, layer 20 writes its KV for every token, then layer 20 and layers 21–39 run on each request's last 128 tokens. The final `mhc_post` runs on that replay batch. Decode graphs stay on the full batch. #59532's replay graphs are already used: the AMD model uses `DeepseekV41ModelState`.

The AMD attention class does not override `forward_kv`. Replay calls `DeepseekV4Attention.forward_kv`, which writes the uint8 SWA cache through `fused_deepseek_v4_kv_rope_insert`.

## What changed

- `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/model.py`: `write_kv` on the last KV source, then `DecoderReplayLayers` from that layer. Pass `write_kv`, the attention metadata prefixes, and that layer's SWA prefix. `mhc_post` runs inside the replay batch. The return is `(hidden_states, pre_mix, *aux)`. The aux state at the cut is captured on the trimmed rows.
- `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/rocm.py`: no `forward_kv` override. The shared method calls `fused_deepseek_v4_kv_rope_insert` and then the compressor insert and indexer K write.
- `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/vl_model.py`: forward `decoder_replay_layers` from the language model.
- `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model_state.py`: when decoder replay layers exist and the prefix-cache window is 0, build `replay_start` and warm the gather kernel. The pad kernel stays on the prefix-cache path.
- Tests cover a 300-token forward (trim, both `mhc_post` calls, the cut-aux capture, the prefix set from the cut, and the SWA insert) and window 0 warming gather without the pad kernel.

## Gating

On when `cache_config.swa_bounded_replay` is set and the v2 model runner is in use. Off with `--no-swa-bounded-replay`. The last KV source must have `compress_ratio <= 1`, and no Engram layer may sit at or after it. ROCm does not read `swa_cache_layer.bounded_replay`; that flag is the prefix-cache path, and attention forces it off. CUDA still requires it. Replay graphs follow `compilation_config.cudagraph_decoder_replay` (default on) and `decoder_replay_trim_threshold` (default 768).

## Depends on

#59894 is in this base. It replaced the row buffers with `write_kv` and `first_swa_prefix`, and replay starts at the last KV source. #56638 is in this base. It replaced #59136 and bounds the ROCm prefill SWA indices at the replay start. #59532 is in this base and supplies the replay graphs. None of the three are in this diff.

## Performance

4× MI325X (gfx942), TP4, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, spec decode off, prefix cache off, HIP INT4 QuickReduce, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`. `max_num_seqs` left at the default. Head `bf6a231a018d`, rebased onto main `c75cb63cd2bb`. The bench, GSM8K, and NIAH below were measured before that rebase and were not re-run. The extension is the installed ROCm nightly `0.31.1rc1.dev1+gbb87d227d`.

Serve log: `Decoder SWA bounded replay: in eager prefill steps, layer 20 writes its KV for every token, and the rest of it and layers 21-39 run on each request's last 128 tokens only.` Also `cudagraph_decoder_replay: True` and `Capturing decoder replay CUDA graphs (PIECEWISE): 4/4`.

4 prompts, 16384 in, 128 out, concurrency 1, seed 7. Both arms completed 4 requests.

| Metric | Replay off | Replay on |
|---|---:|---:|
| Median TTFT | 1176.37 ms | 629.97 ms (−46.4%) |
| Mean TTFT | 1176.09 ms | 629.65 ms (−46.5%) |
| Median TPOT | 10.59 ms | 10.58 ms |
| Mean TPOT | 10.59 ms | 10.58 ms |
| Output throughput | 50.75 tok/s | 64.87 tok/s (+27.8%) |

## Accuracy

RULER `niah_single_2` was not re-run after this drop. On the previous head, 500 samples at 16384 tokens scored 1.0 off and 1.0 on. 65536 was not run.

The 300-token forward wrote the same uint8 SWA cache as `fused_deepseek_v4_kv_rope_insert`. That write covers full blocks and a 12-token tail, and the spare block stayed at the poison value.

GSM8K, 5-shot, 1319 questions, concurrency 8, spec decode off, prefix cache off, `max_num_seqs` at the default:

| Metric | Replay off | Replay on |
|---|---:|---:|
| strict-match | 0.9287 ± 0.0071 | 0.9257 ± 0.0072 |
| flexible-extract | 0.9280 ± 0.0071 | 0.9257 ± 0.0072 |

## Test result

```
11 passed, 14 warnings in 8.17s
```

`test_deepseek_v41_amd_replay_forward.py` and `test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py`, on GPU 4, after the rebase.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Mono decode on every backbone layer
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Follow-up to #60397. The DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash mono decode kernels (MI355X, `--monokernel`) now run all 40 backbone layers whole as K1 + K2. Before, 30 layers ran whole and the other 10 kept vLLM's attention plus the FFN launch: layer 0, the Engram layer 1, and the index sources 2, 8, 14, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36. The switch is now `--monokernel` (`KernelConfig.monokernel`, per RFC #60904), replacing the `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE` environment variable from #60397.

## Claims

- AgentX at TP4, concurrency 1, 3,600 s, Rust frontend, against `main` with mono on: P90 interactivity goes from **541.6 to 562.6 tokens/s/user** (+3.9%), P50 from 569.8 to 595.5 (+4.5%), and ITL p50 from 1.760 to 1.680 ms.
- Accuracy is unchanged. GPQA-Diamond and AIME25 pass@1, mono on against off on this branch, differ by +0.1 ± 0.7 and +1.7 ± 1.2 points, both within noise. RULER NIAH scores 1.00 with mono on and off at 32K, 128K and 256K.
- Nothing changes with the switch off, and the 30 standard layers build the same kernels as before.

## Validation

**Performance.** MI355X, TP4, DSpark with 5 drafts and synthetic acceptance 3.51 (InferenceX#3690's TP4 recipe), AgentX at concurrency 1. Each arm is one 3,600 s run, and both arms ran at the same time on GPUs 0–3 and 4–7.

| | P90 interactivity | P50 interactivity | ITL p50 | TTFT p50 | requests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `main` (7d0b4e57aa), mono on | 541.6 | 569.8 | 1.760 ms | 0.200 s | 328 |
| this PR, mono on | **562.6** | **595.5** | **1.680 ms** | 0.201 s | 332 |

The `main` arm reproduces InferenceX's sweep point for this config (543). A 900 s run of each arm on the Python frontend gave +6.2% on P90 (503.5 to 534.5).

**Accuracy.** TP2, this branch, mono on against off, 4 seeds each, thinking on, DSpark with block rejection. Each mono-on server logged every backbone layer running whole.

| | mono on | mono off | on − off (paired by question) |
|---|---|---|---|
| GPQA-Diamond pass@1 | 85.0 ± 2.2 | 85.0 ± 2.2 | +0.1 ± 0.7 |
| AIME25 pass@1 | 100.0 ± 0.0 | 98.3 ± 1.2 | +1.7 ± 1.2 |

**Long context.** RULER NIAH, TP2, this branch, mono on against off: single-1, multikey-2 and multikey-3 at 32K, 128K and 256K, 40 samples each, greedy. All 9 points score 1.00 on both arms (360 samples per arm).

**Tests**, all run locally on MI355X:

- `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py` at TP2 and TP4: passed. Its 5-layer model now covers every variant: the first layer, a ratio-2 KV and index source, a ratio-2 consumer with an Engram, a ratio-1 KV, index and candidate source, and a ratio-1 index source over layer 3's candidates. Every layer has to take the whole-layer path on every rank at every decode step.
- `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py` at TP2 and TP4, including the 300-replay CUDA-graph stress: passed.
- `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py`: 37 passed.
- `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` on the 5-layer model with CUDA graphs: no sync in steady-state decode. The runner's one-time setup on the first decode step syncs, as on `main`.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py -v
# AgentX: InferenceX#3690 dsv41flash TP4 c1 recipe with --monokernel, `infx.bench agentic`, DURATION=3600
# Evals: lm-eval local-chat-completions on GPQA-Diamond / AIME25, temperature 0.6, top_p 0.95, 4 seeds, mono on vs off
# NIAH: lm-eval RULER niah_single_1 / niah_multikey_2 / niah_multikey_3 (chat), max_seq_lengths 32768 / 131072 / 262144, --limit 40
```
</details>

## Details

- **Settled residual (layers 0, 1, 14).** K1 gets a `fold` build flag. Without it, the seam slice takes the residual as it arrives instead of folding the previous layer's output in. Layer 0's residual is the embedding broadcast to the 4 streams, with an identity incoming pre-mix. The mix projection uses `hc_attn_fn` over the broadcast, which equals vLLM's folded `hc_attn_fn_broadcast` up to summation order. On an Engram layer, `mhc_post` and the Engram write run in torch before K1, as on vLLM's path.
- **Index sources (layers 2, 8, 14, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36).** K1 gets an `index` build flag.
  - K1 also stores its normed input and its bf16 qr (the q_norm output). It skips the key-table stage, because the top-k does not exist yet.
  - Between the two launches, `_select` runs vLLM's own modules: the compressor and its cache insert, the indexer K write, `weights_proj`, `forward_q` and `indexer_op`.
  - K2 then builds the key table on its last CTAs. Each attention split task waits on its token's flag, and the table goes through device scope, since the same launch reads it.
- **Tradeoffs.**
  - The compressor and indexer now run serially between the kernels. vLLM's path overlapped them on side streams, which the persistent kernels can't do, since they need every CU.
  - The indexer's `wq_b` quantizes the bf16 qr itself, where vLLM's fused q-norm hands it fp8 qr. The model-level test bounds the difference.
  - `_select` restates the module call sequence of `_forward_csa2_full` and `_forward_csa2_reindex` without their stream forks.
- **Not covered.** The DSpark draft layers still take vLLM's path. A layer outside the kernels (an MXFP8 KV cache, another indexer type) still takes the FFN launch, and the model-level test no longer exercises that launch; the numerics test does.
- **Model-level test bounds.**
  - Layer 0 now runs whole, so its output is held to 3% at every token. The old 1.5% at a request's first decode token was written for the FFN launch.
  - The near-tie exemption past layer 0 widens from 5e-3 to 1e-2. Every layer's input now carries the earlier layers' kernel differences (0.4–0.7%). One TP4 token flipped an expert at a gap of 0.0072 while every other token stayed near 4%.
- **Relation to other PRs.** #60731 ports the mono kernels to gfx942 and touches the same files. The two don't overlap in function, but whichever merges second needs a rebase.
- **Remaining gap.** On the formal sweep, ATOM's P90 at this point is 574. Moving the indexer's scoring and top-k, and the draft layers, into the kernels are the next steps.

commits.pr_title: [Model Loader] Make dummy weight init dtype-aware
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Make `--load-format dummy` produce non-degenerate quantized weights by picking dummy values per dtype in `initialize_single_dummy_weight`. Today, dummy-loaded MXFP4 MoE experts are entirely zero and FP8 weights are ~98% zero. That skews performance measurements with dummy weights (e.g. MoE routing and kernels see all-zero experts).

Related: #54958 bounds the memory of the FP8 dummy path. It's complementary (how values are generated vs. which values), and this PR keeps that code path intact so the two compose.

## Claims

- uint8 / int8 / `float4_e2m1fn_x2` params (packed FP4, int8 weights and zero points) get deterministic random bytes instead of being left as zeros or uninitialized memory. Every FP4 code is finite.
- E8M0 scales (`float8_e8m0fnu`, or uint8 params named like a scale, e.g. MXFP4 `w13_weight_scale`) get a fixed 2**-7 instead of arbitrary tiny exponents.
- 8-bit floats default to the range ±1 instead of ±1e-3, which mostly underflows in FP8 (E4M3's smallest normal is 2**-6).
- Wider integer params (int32/int64, e.g. `g_idx`) are untouched, since random values could be out-of-range indices. Explicit `low`/`high` and `dummy_weight_value` still take precedence.

## Validation

Weight statistics after `LLM(model, load_format="dummy")` (after `process_weights_after_loading`) on GB200, measured with `llm.apply_model`:

| Model | Param dtype | Zero fraction before | Zero fraction after | Non-finite |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `RedHatAI/gpt-oss-20b` (MXFP4 experts) | uint8 (packed FP4 + scales) | 1.0 | 0.0039 (≈1/256) | 0 |
| `RedHatAI/gpt-oss-20b` | float8_e4m3fn (backend-converted) | 1.0 | 0.0 | 0 |
| `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8` | float8_e4m3fn | 0.977 | 0.001 | 0 |

Both models generate with finite logprobs before and after.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction script</summary>

```python
import sys, torch
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

def weight_stats(model):
    stats = {}
    for _, p in model.named_parameters():
        if p.dtype in (torch.bfloat16, torch.float16, torch.float32):
            continue
        s = stats.setdefault(str(p.dtype), [0, 0])
        raw = p.data.view(torch.uint8) if p.dtype in (torch.uint8, torch.int8) else p.data.float()
        s[0] += int((raw == 0).sum()); s[1] += p.numel()
    return {k: round(z / n, 4) for k, (z, n) in stats.items()}

llm = LLM(sys.argv[1], load_format="dummy", enforce_eager=True, max_model_len=1024,
          gpu_memory_utilization=0.5, skip_tokenizer_init=True)
print(llm.apply_model(weight_stats)[0])
print(llm.generate([{"prompt_token_ids": [785, 6722, 315, 9625, 374]}],
                   SamplingParams(max_tokens=8, temperature=0, logprobs=1))[0].outputs[0].logprobs)
```

Run with `VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION=1`.
</details>

Unit tests (run in CI by `.buildkite/test_areas/model_executor.yaml`):

```
pytest tests/model_executor/test_weight_utils.py -q
42 passed
```

New tests cover the FP8 range, fixed E8M0 scales (both dtypes), deterministic random bytes for uint8/int8/FP4, and wide integer params left untouched.

No model evaluation: real checkpoint loading is unaffected. Only `--load-format dummy` values change.

## Details

- **Identifying uint8 E8M0 scales by name.** Several quant methods (MXFP4, Quark OCP-MX, ModelOpt MXFP8) store E8M0 scales as uint8, which is indistinguishable from packed weights by dtype. `DummyModelLoader` now passes each tensor's attribute name, and uint8 tensors whose name contains `scale` get the E8M0 fill. Quant methods can still override per param with `dummy_weight_value`.
- **Magnitudes.** 2**-7 keeps dequantized weights small and finite: |FP4| ≤ 6 gives ≤ 0.047; FP8 ±1 gives ≤ 0.008. FP8 weights with float32 scales (dummy ±1e-3) end up around ±1e-3, matching bf16 dummies.
- **ROCm** previously zeroed all integer params for cross-process reproducibility. 8-bit integer params are now filled from the seeded generator, which is also reproducible.
- **Limitation.** GGUF block formats are uint8 with embedded fp16 scales, so random bytes can decode to large or non-finite values. That's no worse than the uninitialized memory they got before.
- **Behavior change.** Benchmarks run with dummy weights on FP8 / MXFP4 / int8 models may shift, because their quantized weights are no longer zero.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][MLA] Keep DCP prefill context in FP8 through AllGather
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Keep ROCm MLA's cached DCP context in FP8 through AllGather, then use AITER's fused gather/projection kernel to expand it into K/V. This removes the BF16 communication payload and separate reorganization, dequantization, projection and packing operations for supported configurations.

```diff
 local cached context
-  gather/dequant → BF16 AllGather → reorg → kv_b_proj → K/V pack
+  gather bytes → FP8 AllGather → fused reorg/dequant/kv_b_proj/K/V pack
```

## Claims

- Halves AllGather bytes for the same padded row count, preserving the existing FP8 cache bytes, workspace capacity, chunking and merge plan.
- Falls back to the original path for unsupported cache formats, dimensions, dtypes or projection layouts. The optional upstream K/V concatenation callback is forwarded on that fallback.
- Historical full-model K3 measurements below show unchanged aggregate GSM8K accuracy and lower cached-prefix TTFT with **both this PR and #59069**. Those measurements do not isolate this PR's end-to-end contribution or validate the current rebased head.

## Validation

| Full GSM8K | Original context path | Fused context path |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Strict match | **1264/1319 (95.8302%)** | **1263/1319 (95.7544%)** |
| Flexible extract | **1264/1319 (95.8302%)** | **1263/1319 (95.7544%)** |

commits.pr_title: [Attention][Spec Decode] Multi-query Triton split-K for spec-decode verify, with empty-segment/padding hardening
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose

Spec-decode verify runs attention with a few query tokens per request (1+K). On `main`, the Triton backend admits only `max_seqlen_q == 1` to the 3D split-K kernel, so verify batches fall back to the 2D kernel, which parallelizes only over Q blocks and gets slow at long context and low batch. This PR lets short multi-query batches use split-K, with a shape-only gate in `unified_attention`: split-K runs when `max_seqlen_q <= 8` and `num_seqs * cdiv(max_seqlen_q, BLOCK_Q) <= seq_threshold_3D` (identical to `main` for `max_seqlen_q == 1`). There is no uniform-decode detection or platform special case; non-causal, per-sequence-causal and mm-prefix masking and the SM100 head-256 path stay on 2D. It also makes split-K exact for fully masked tiles, empty segments and CUDA-graph padding rows.

## Changes

- `triton_unified_attention.py`: the shape-only 3D gate above; launch-time scratch check with 2D fallback.
- `triton_attention_helpers.py`: `softmax_step` no longer clamps a fully masked tile's −inf running max to 0; `reduce_segments` skips empty/unvisited segments and returns early for padding rows and `seq_len <= 0`.
- `triton_attn.py`: split-K scratch sized per query token, `min(seq_threshold_3D, max_num_seqs) * (1+K)` rows (`1+2K` with parallel drafting, only when ≤ 8), composed with #58482's 64-segment row cap on SM12.0.
- Tests: speculative split-K vs reference incl. FP8 query (asserting split-K ran), padding/empty-segment cases, scratch sizing, 64-segment row coverage for verify batches.

## Results

Kernel, c1-tp8 MiniMax-M3 shape (8 q / 1 KV head, FP8 KV, width 6, one request), 2D → split-K, µs (16 segments; measured before the #58482 composition commit):

| Context | SM120 | H200 |
|---|---:|---:|
| 4k | 142.9 → 22.6 | 165.8 → 24.5 |
| 128k | 4327 → 444 | 6187 → 537 |

Across 1736 multi-query shapes per GPU (widths 2–8, BF16/FP8 KV), split-K matches the reference; 7/1370 (SM120) and 18/1370 (H200) admitted shapes are >3% slower than 2D (worst 1.08× / 1.21×), all at the threshold edge.

E2E, MiniMax-M3-NVFP4 + EAGLE3 on 8× RTX PRO 6000 (with #59081, #57197, #56151, #58482), this PR vs. its earlier uniform-decode-gated revision. Ratios; throughput tok/s/GPU, interactivity p90; ±3% rule set before each run:

| Config | Runs | Throughput | Interactivity | Verdict |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| c1, TP8, K=5 (width 6) | n=1 | 0.998 | 1.007 | pass |
| c10, TP8, K=3 | n=1 | 0.995 | 0.962 | **FAIL** |
| c10, TP8, K=3 | n=4 per arm | 1.000 [0.996, 1.003] | 0.984 [0.947, 1.036] | equivalent (≥ 0.97) |

These E2E runs predate the #58482 composition commit, which changes only SM12.0 scratch sizing. At c1 every width-6 verify launch on all ranks ran split-K. At c10, 3 of 4 runs of this PR had lower interactivity than every run of the earlier revision, so a few-percent cost is not ruled out. Earlier revision vs. `main` (same split-K admission for uniform verify): Llama-3.1-8B EAGLE3 16k c1 +91.5% tok/s on SM120, +145% on H100; GSM8K equivalent. That earlier revision also had regressions vs. `main` at Llama SM120 16k c64 and Gemma-4 8192/c16; not re-measured on this head.

E2E on B300 (SM103), MiniMax-M3-NVFP4 + EAGLE3, `TRITON_ATTN`, TP1, this PR vs. `main` at the merge base, 3 interleaved runs per arm (on this GPU family only the 3 dense layers and the EAGLE3 draft use `unified_attention`; the sparse layers use MSA):

| Workload | Throughput | Interactivity | Median TPOT (ms) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| c1, K=5 (width 6), ISL 205k | **1.642×** [1.641, 1.643] | **2.112×** [2.107, 2.116] | 15.29 → 7.24 |
| c10, K=3 (width 4), ISL 111k | 1.019× [1.018, 1.022] | 1.037× [1.034, 1.041] | 28.50 → 27.49 |

At c10 (closed-loop), median TTFT was higher with this PR (11.97 s vs 10.66 s); with a fixed open-loop arrival schedule it is at parity (paired median TTFT ratio 0.990 [0.988, 0.995], prefill time unchanged), so this was a closed-loop turnover effect. B200 not measured.

## Tests

- `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_unified_attention.py tests/v1/attention/test_triton_attn_segments.py` on SM12.0 and H200: no status changes vs. the previous head on shared tests; the only failures are the 290 pre-existing `test_triton_unified_attn_use_td*` cases, which also fail on `main`. Mutation-checked (row-capacity fallback, padding early return, scratch sizing).
- `pytest tests/quantization/test_per_token_kv_cache.py` (other `reduce_segments` caller): same results as `main` (3 pre-existing INT4 failures on both).
- `pre-commit run --all-files` and `pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual`: pass.

## Notes

- **Memory:** scratch grows for spec decode, e.g. MiniMax-M3 TP8 +24 MiB (K=3) / +42 MiB (K=5) per Triton metadata builder per rank; non-spec ≤ `main`. Computed, not measured; like `main`'s scratch it is allocated after KV-cache profiling.
- **Behavior change:** eager non-uniform decode batches (e.g. 10 requests / 12 tokens) now take split-K instead of 2D; this is the likely source of the c10 difference above. Keeping them on 2D is a one-line gate change.
- **Not validated:** ROCm/XPU; E2E on SM80/89/100 and non-spec workloads on this head; R-SWA, DFlash, VLM mm_prefix.
- **Overlap:** #44652, #45450, #46724, #52879 and #57409 touch the same 3D gate/scratch; comparison in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52049#issuecomment-5804025232. This PR differs by the shape-only gate plus the masked-tile/padding fixes, which we can fold into whichever PR maintainers prefer.

**AI assistance:** Claude Code and other coding agents (OpenAI Codex, Devin, Cursor) wrote code and tests, ran and analyzed GPU validation, and drafted this description. The human submitter is responsible for every changed line.

- [x] The submitting human has reviewed every changed line and run the validations listed above.

commits.pr_title: [MoE] Add MoNe experts pruning support
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Mixture of Novices and Experts (MoNe) is an expert pruning method accepted at ICLR-2026 https://arxiv.org/pdf/2507.00390
 
The method computes statistics (access frequency and output variance) about experts during calibration, identifies redundant experts and replaces them with constant vectors which are their unbiased estimators. MoNe is planned to be supported in the llm-compressor https://github.com/vllm-project/llm-compressor/pull/2906 

Implementation
- Defines a generic expert-substitution format in compression_config.
- Supports constant-v1, where a substituted expert returns a stored constant vector while keeping its original router weight.
- Automatically detects compatible MoE layers and loads only retained expert weights, preserving the GPU memory saving.
- Provides a default path for compatible decomposed MoE backends by sending substituted routes with zero weights.
- Validates checkpoint metadata and tensor loading, including tensor-parallel correctness.
Models using the standard FusedMoEFactory and RoutedExperts loading path do not need architecture-specific changes.

commits.pr_body:
Implements the per-request `metrics` (`--enable-per-request-metrics`) roadmap item in #44280. Speculative-decoding acceptance stats remain a separate checklist item.

## Summary

- Accept `--enable-per-request-metrics` in the Rust frontend and reject it alongside `--disable-log-stats`.
- Carry the engine's queue, schedule, first-token, and last-token timestamps through decoded text and chat output.
- Return Python-compatible timing fields in non-streaming `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/completions` responses. For streaming, attach them to the final usage chunk when `stream_options.include_usage` is enabled.
- Serialize unavailable timing fields as `null` in non-streaming responses and omit them from streaming usage chunks, matching Python's recursive `exclude_none=True` behavior.

## Implementation detail

Each engine output carries the current request-timestamp snapshot. This is required because the Rust text decoder can terminate a request locally after matching a stop string, before the engine emits a terminal output. Keeping the snapshot with the current output lets that path report valid metrics; limiting timestamps to engine-terminal outputs caused the Rust frontend to panic in Buildkite CI. The snapshot is four `f64` values and does not add GPU synchronization.

## Scope

Speculative-decoding acceptance metrics are intentionally not included in this PR. `GenerateOutput` already carries terminal `spec_decode_metrics`, but mapping those values into the OpenAI `PerRequestMetrics.speculative_decoding` response field is separate follow-up work.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KVConnector] Fix MoRI-IO WRITE-mode requests stranded in WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

In MoRI-IO WRITE (push) mode, decode requests can get stuck in `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` forever when decode is overloaded. The engine stays healthy and keeps serving new requests, so this shows up as a benchmark that never finishes rather than as an error. At 1024 in / 1024 out, 128 requests at concurrency 64, with decode limited to 20 running requests, runs on `main` stall before all requests finish.

This PR fixes two causes. A third cause, decode preemption, is fixed by #53250. This PR used to include the same change, but it has been removed in favour of that PR.

### 1. Prefill gives up on a deferred write without telling decode

In push mode the proxy sends each request to prefill and decode at the same time. Prefill computes the KV cache and then waits for decode to allocate blocks and send their IDs. If decode is busy, the request can wait in decode's queue for longer than `defer_timeout` (60 s). On `main`, prefill then frees its blocks and drops the write, but never tells decode. When decode later admits the request, it waits for KV that will never arrive.

Now, when a deferred write times out:

- Prefill marks the transfer as finished under the lock, so a late block allocation from decode is ignored and no write can start. If the allocation arrived just before the timeout, the write goes ahead as normal.
- Prefill sends `write_failed` to every decode DP rank. Prefill never received the allocation, so it cannot know which rank owns the request. Ranks that do not own it ignore the message, and decode keeps only a bounded number of unmatched failures.
- Prefill then releases its blocks, even if sending a notification failed. This is safe because no write was ever issued.
- Decode reports the request as a failed KV load. It is then failed or recomputed according to `kv_load_failure_policy`. Because no write was issued, decode can free its blocks straight away.

The prefill scheduler no longer has its own WRITE-mode timeout that freed blocks on its own. Only the worker releases them, after the transfer is marked finished.

### 2. A full local prefix-cache hit sent an empty block list

When decode already had the whole prompt in its prefix cache, it sent prefill an empty block list. Prefill rejects that with `MoRIIOError("block_notify_list cannot be empty")` and keeps its blocks. Decode now sends a release message instead, so prefill frees them.

### Related PRs

- #53250 stops a preempted decode request from waiting for a second push. Under the overload above, decode preemption also strands requests, so this PR relies on #53250 to fully fix the hang. With `kv_load_failure_policy=recompute`, #53250 is also what lets a failed request recompute locally.
- #58962 adds a receive timeout on decode for when prefill dies mid-transfer. In that case decode cannot know whether a write is still in flight, so it keeps the blocks. The two PRs cover different failures: this one handles a live prefill that never started the write, and #58962 handles a prefill that cannot send anything.

## Test Plan

Unit tests, which need neither ROCm nor the `mori` package:

```

pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio*.py
```

End-to-end reproduction in WRITE mode with the `xgmi` backend. Start the proxy first so both engines can register:

```bash
python examples/disaggregated/disaggregated_serving/moriio_toy_proxy_server.py --port 8402
```

```bash
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 vllm serve meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \
  --port 8400 \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{
    "kv_connector": "MoRIIOConnector",
    "kv_role": "kv_producer",
    "kv_connector_extra_config": {
      "backend": "xgmi",
      "read_mode": false,
      "proxy_ip": "127.0.0.1",
      "proxy_ping_port": "36367",
      "http_port": "8400",
      "handshake_port": "8600",
      "notify_port": "8500"
    }
  }'
```

```bash
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 vllm serve meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \
  --port 8401 \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --max-num-seqs 20 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{
    "kv_connector": "MoRIIOConnector",
    "kv_role": "kv_consumer",
    "kv_connector_extra_config": {
      "backend": "xgmi",
      "read_mode": false,

```

```bash
  --endpoint /v1/completions --model meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --num-prompts 128 --max-concurrency 64 --seed 8088 --ignore-eos
```

`--max-num-seqs 20` makes decode the bottleneck so that some requests wait longer than `defer_timeout`. Add `"kv_load_failure_policy": "recompute"` to the decode config to have timed-out requests recomputed instead of failed.

## Test Result

All 207 MoRI-IO unit tests pass on ROCm with `mori` installed (204 on `main`, plus 3 new). The new tests, in the CPU-only `test_moriio_write_done_routing.py`, cover:

- an expired deferred write: the transfer is marked finished, prefill blocks are released, `write_failed` reaches every decode DP rank across pods, and a late allocation is ignored
- the prefill scheduler waiting for the worker's ACK instead of freeing WRITE blocks on its own timeout
- decode reporting `write_failed` as a failed KV load on the rank that owns the request

End-to-end, using the commands above with #53250 applied (2× Radeon AI Pro R9700S, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct), the benchmark finishes and KV cache usage returns to zero on both prefill and decode:

| `recompute` | 128 | 0 | 34 |

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Parser] Stop re-parsing the whole GLM tool argument per chunk
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Streaming a GLM tool call re-parses the whole argument on every chunk, so a long argument (for example a 100 KB file `Write`) costs quadratic CPU on the API server. This PR streams the open argument value with work proportional to each chunk.

Related: #51141 fixes the same pattern for the Inkling parser only (compared under Details).

## Claims

- Parser cost per streamed GLM argument chunk no longer grows with argument length: 6.4 ms at 100 KB and 12.7 ms at 200 KB become 7 us at every size (M4 Pro, table below).
- Streamed deltas are unchanged, including schema type coercion and the held-back trailing value for non-string keys.
- Opt-in per parser through a new `ParserEngineConfig.arg_value_extender`. Only `glm47_moe` (GLM-4.7 and later, including GLM-5.x) sets it. Every other parser keeps its current path.
- Model evaluation does not apply, since model output and streamed tool-call text are unchanged.

## Validation

Tests on `691b6c37c`:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pytest tests/parser/engine` | 5869 passed |
| `pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_glm47_moe_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_glm4_moe_tool_parser.py tests/reasoning/test_glm4_moe_reasoning_parser.py` | 39 passed |
| pre-commit on the changed files | passed |

New tests in `tests/parser/engine/test_glm47_moe.py`:
- `test_long_call_streams_non_streaming_arguments`: a 26 KB GLM call with escapes, non-ASCII and tag-like text, streamed in 7-character chunks through `parse_delta`, gives the same arguments as `extract_tool_calls`. Runs with no schema and with a schema that coerces an integer key.
- `test_conversions_do_not_grow_with_argument_length`: counts streaming calls to the arg converter. With this PR the count is 23 for both 40 and 400 lines of content. On `main` it is 547 and 5,227, so the test fails there.
- Two small tests for the GLM extender: a closing tag split across chunks, and the cases where no extender is created.

**Same output as `main`.** A local differential test streamed 15,000 random GLM tool calls through `main`'s parser and this branch. It used random chunk sizes; schemas with string, integer, object, array, boolean and nullable keys; repeated keys; truncated calls; and tag fragments inside values. Every per-chunk `DeltaMessage` was identical. Both new paths ran: per 3,000 cases, about 100K chunks extended a streamed string value and about 57K extended a held-back value. The same check passed on 6,000 more cases with the GLM regexes from #54971 applied to both sides.

**Per-chunk cost.** The script below streams a GLM `Write` call through `Glm47MoeParser.parse_delta` in 8-character chunks. Each row is the mean cost per chunk since the previous row. Apple M4 Pro, Python 3.12, 3 runs each, range across runs.

| Argument size | `main` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 25 KB | 1.04-1.06 ms | 6.9-7.1 us |
| 50 KB | 3.11-3.17 ms | 7.0-7.1 us |
| 100 KB | 6.37-6.44 ms | 6.9-7.0 us |
| 200 KB | 12.68-12.79 ms | 6.8-7.0 us |

`_compute_arg_delta` alone, timed with a script that drives the extracted parser functions, goes from 6.7 ms to 0.9 us per chunk at 100 KB and from 13.3 ms to 0.95 us at 200 KB, with byte-identical streamed arguments.

**Replay at serving step rate.** A 115 KB Python-file `Write` call, tokenized with the GLM-5.3 tokenizer, replayed through the streaming lexer and `_compute_arg_delta` at 22.4 decode steps/s and 2.8 tokens per step (the rate measured on a GLM-5.3 decode server). Parser CPU per 30 s of stream climbs from 0.008 to 0.20 cores on `main` over the 6.3-minute stream. With this PR it stays between 0.00006 and 0.00008 cores. The streamed arguments are byte-identical.

<details>
<summary>Reproducer</summary>

Run from the root of a vLLM checkout:

```python
import time
from unittest.mock import MagicMock

from tests.parser.engine.conftest import make_mock_tokenizer
from vllm.entrypoints.openai.chat_completion.protocol import ChatCompletionRequest
from vllm.parser.glm47_moe import Glm47MoeParser

vocab = {"<think>": 1, "</think>": 2, "<tool_call>": 3, "</tool_call>": 4}
request = MagicMock(spec=ChatCompletionRequest)
request.tools, request.tool_choice, request.include_reasoning = [], "auto", True
parser = Glm47MoeParser(make_mock_tokenizer(vocab))

head = (
    "</think><tool_call>Write<arg_key>file_path</arg_key>"
    "<arg_value>/repo/app.py</arg_value><arg_key>content</arg_key><arg_value>"
)
body = (open("vllm/sampling_params.py").read() * 10)[:200_000]
parser.parse_delta(head, [], request, finished=False)

marks, elapsed, chunks = [25_000, 50_000, 100_000, 200_000], 0.0, 0
for i in range(0, len(body), 8):
    start = time.perf_counter()
    parser.parse_delta(body[i : i + 8], [], request, finished=False)
    elapsed += time.perf_counter() - start
    chunks += 1
    if marks and i + 8 >= marks[0]:
        print(f"{marks.pop(0) // 1000} KB: {elapsed / chunks * 1e6:.1f} us per chunk")
        elapsed, chunks = 0.0, 0
```

</details>

## Details

**Trigger.** Any streamed GLM tool call with a long argument, for example a coding agent writing a file.

**Mechanism.** `_compute_arg_delta` runs once per `ARG_VALUE_CHUNK`. Each run works on the whole argument received so far:
- joins `slot.args`;
- runs `_glm47_arg_converter`: three regex passes and `json.dumps`;
- runs `_fix_arg_types`: `json.loads`;
- runs `_safe_arg_prefix`: a Python character loop over the whole JSON, 89% of the time under cProfile.

GLM sets `stream_arg_deltas=True` and no `arg_structural_chars`, so every chunk takes this path.

**Effect.** Cost per chunk grows linearly with the argument, so one tool call costs quadratic time. It runs inside `parse_delta` on the API server's event loop, so it also delays other requests on that server.

**Why the fix is in `engine/`.** The full conversion per chunk lives in `ParserEngine._compute_arg_delta`. Every parser that sets `arg_converter` and streams deltas without `arg_structural_chars` runs it on every chunk: GLM-4.7, Granite, Inkling, MiniMax-M2, Nemotron-v3, Qwen3 and Step-3.5. The engine part is a generic opt-in hook, and the format knowledge stays in each parser's file. This PR wires GLM only.

**Fix.**
- After a full conversion, once the safe prefix is sent, the engine calls `arg_value_extender(slot.args)`. It returns an extender for the open trailing value, or `None`.
- For each later chunk, the extender returns the JSON text the chunk appends to that value, or `None` when the chunk may change anything else. On `None`, the engine runs the full conversion as today, which may create a new extender.
- `_safe_arg_prefix` also reports whether the open value streams. If it does, the engine sends the extender's text. If the value is held back (non-string key), it sends nothing, as today.
- `ToolCallSlot.streamed_json` keeps its parts in a list and joins them on read, like `args`, so the fast path does no work proportional to the argument.

Full conversions now happen only around argument boundaries.

**Why the GLM extender gives the same output.**
- The open value runs to the end of the raw arguments, and the converter emits it as a JSON string with `json.dumps`. JSON string escaping maps each character on its own, so a chunk appends `json.dumps(chunk)[1:-1]`.
- A chunk can only change the parse by completing `</arg_value>`. The extender keeps the last 11 raw characters, so it also sees a closing tag split across chunks.
- The extender is only created when the open key is the last key of the parsed arguments. A repeated earlier key updates an earlier position, so that case falls back to the full conversion.
- Schema coercion leaves string keys alone and coerces earlier values the same way every time, so the JSON before the open value stays the same.

**Overlapping PRs** (checked 2026-10-12).
- #51141 (Inkling) caches the wrapper offset, scans the safe prefix incrementally, and sets `arg_structural_chars`. Its scan resumes from the previous end of the JSON. That fits Inkling, whose converter returns a growing slice of the raw text. The GLM converter closes the JSON (`"}`) again on every chunk, so it needs a different approach. I think Inkling could implement `arg_value_extender` too, so both parsers share one mechanism; we can align with #51141 on the order.
- #54971 changes only the GLM key regexes. The extender reuses `_ARG_RE` and `_PARTIAL_ARG_RE`, and its close check depends only on `</arg_value>`, so it works with either version (differential above).
- #53739 and #58780 also edit `_compute_arg_delta` or `_safe_arg_prefix`, so whichever lands second needs a rebase.

**Limitations.** All measurements drive the parser code directly. There is no end-to-end run on a GPU serving deployment.

**AI assistance.** Claude Code was used for the implementation, tests and measurements.

commits.pr_title: [Docs] Fix broken llm-d.ai links on the llm-d integration page
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Every llm-d.ai documentation link on the [llm-d integration page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/deployment/integrations/llm-d/) returns 404. This repoints all nine at their current published URLs. Docs only, no link text changed.

## Claims

- Fixes 9 broken links (all returning 404) on `docs/deployment/integrations/llm-d.md`.
- No remaining `llm-d.ai` link on the page 404s.
- Link text and prose are untouched, so the rendered page reads identically.

## Validation

Before, every one of these was a 404:

```console
https://llm-d.ai/docs/guides                                 404
https://llm-d.ai/docs/guides/precise-prefix-cache-aware      404
https://llm-d.ai/docs/guides/tiered-prefix-cache             404
https://llm-d.ai/docs/guides/pd-disaggregation               404
https://llm-d.ai/docs/guides/wide-expert-parallelism         404
https://llm-d.ai/docs/guides/workload-autoscaling            404
https://llm-d.ai/docs/guides/flow-control                    404
https://llm-d.ai/docs/guides/optimized-baseline              404
https://llm-d.ai/docs/getting-started                        404
```

After, every `llm-d.ai` link on the page resolves:

```console
$ grep -oE 'https://llm-d\.ai[^)]*' docs/deployment/integrations/llm-d.md | sort -u \
    | while read -r u; do printf '%-80s %s\n' "$u" "$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -L "$u")"; done
https://llm-d.ai/                                                                200
https://llm-d.ai/docs                                                            200
https://llm-d.ai/docs/architecture                                               200
https://llm-d.ai/docs/architecture/advanced/kv-management                        200
https://llm-d.ai/docs/getting-started/quickstart                                 200
https://llm-d.ai/docs/well-lit-paths                                             200
https://llm-d.ai/docs/well-lit-paths/foundations/flow-control                    200
https://llm-d.ai/docs/well-lit-paths/foundations/optimized-baseline              200
https://llm-d.ai/docs/well-lit-paths/foundations/pd-disaggregation               200
https://llm-d.ai/docs/well-lit-paths/foundations/precise-prefix-cache-routing    200
https://llm-d.ai/docs/well-lit-paths/foundations/tiered-prefix-cache             200
https://llm-d.ai/docs/well-lit-paths/foundations/wide-expert-parallelism         200
https://llm-d.ai/docs/well-lit-paths/foundations/workload-autoscaling            200
https://llm-d.ai/slack                                                           200
```

A `grep -c 'docs/guides'` on the file now returns 0, and the only remaining `getting-started` reference is `/getting-started/quickstart`, which is valid.

## Details

Root cause: `/docs/guides/...` has never been a route on llm-d.ai. The `llm-d/llm-d` repository has a top-level `guides/` directory holding deployment recipes (Helm values, scripts), but the website is built from `docs/`, which publishes the well-lit paths under `/docs/well-lit-paths/foundations/`. `git log` on `llm-d/llm-d` confirms no `docs/guides` directory has ever existed, and the llm-d.ai sitemap has no `/docs/guides` entry in any published version (0.7, 0.8, 0.9, current). So these are not links broken by a later rename; they have never resolved.

Two links needed more than the path prefix swap:

| Old | New | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/docs/guides/precise-prefix-cache-aware` | `/docs/well-lit-paths/foundations/precise-prefix-cache-routing` | The page was additionally renamed from `precise-prefix-cache-aware` to `precise-prefix-cache-routing` in llm-d/llm-d#1560. |
| `/docs/guides#advanced-kv-cache-management` | `/docs/architecture/advanced/kv-management` | That anchor does not exist. The topic now has its own page, titled "KV Cache Management". |

Separately, `/docs/getting-started` 404s even though `docs/getting-started/README.mdx` exists, because that file sets `slug: /` and is therefore served at the `/docs` root. The "Introduction" link now points at `/docs`.

Since these URLs were never published, there is nothing for llm-d.ai to redirect from, so the fix belongs here rather than in the llm-d website.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Pace the CRCR nightly report under the relay rate limit
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

The torch-nightly CRCR report (`.buildkite/scripts/crcr_report.py`) posts one callback per Buildkite job, back to back, with no retry. The PyTorch Cross-Repo CI Relay limits callbacks per repo over a sliding 60 s window (`RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN`, currently 100). So every nightly records only the first 100 jobs and the rest get a 429:

| Build | Report |
|---|---|
| [93355](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/93355) | `reported 100 job(s), 244 failed` |
| [93593](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/93593) | `reported 100 job(s), 269 failed` |
| [93820](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/93820) | `reported 100 job(s), 270 failed` |

```
429 for :nvidia: (H100) MLA Kernel Test: {"detail": "rate limit exceeded for vllm-project/vllm"}
```

HUD's CRCR view of vLLM nightlies therefore covers about 27% of the jobs, and which jobs depends on the order Buildkite returns them in. The step is `soft_fail` and exits 0, so nothing flagged it.

## Changes

- **`crcr_report.py`:** wait `CRCR_POST_INTERVAL_S` (default 0.65 s, about 92/min, under the current limit) between callbacks. Retry a 429 with 2/4/8/16/32 s backoff, about 62 s in total so the last attempt lands in a fresh window. A full nightly (~370 jobs) now takes about 4 minutes to report.
- **`crcr-report.sh`:** the post-wait OIDC token is minted with `--lifetime 1800`, because the default five-minute lifetime no longer covers a paced report. If the agent rejects `--lifetime`, it falls back to the old call, so the report is never lost to a flag mismatch.

Relay side: pytorch/test-infra#9096 raises the limit to 300/min/repo and adds the same 429 retry to the GitHub Actions reporter. Once that is deployed, `CRCR_POST_INTERVAL_S` can be lowered.

## Test Plan

Ran `crcr_report.py` against a local fake relay:
- Responses 200, 429, 429, then 200: the second job retried after 2 s and 4 s, and all 4 jobs were reported (`reported 4 job(s), 0 failed`).
- 429 every time, with backoff shortened: every job was logged as `429 for …` after its retries, `reported 0 job(s), 4 failed`, exit 0 (best-effort, unchanged).

`ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `bash -n` and `shellcheck` are clean.

## Test Result

The next torch-nightly run (`TORCH_NIGHTLY=1` on main) should log `reported <all> job(s), 0 failed` for the CRCR step.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf] Fix Gemma AR+RMS prefill fallback
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

1. Teach the AITER compilation pass to preserve raw Gemma weights and pass `gemma_norm` through the fused all-reduce op.
2. When custom all-reduce rejects a large prefill tensor, run the regular all-reduce followed by AITER's fused-add RMSNorm (the registered `vllm_aiter.fused_add_rms_norm` op, which gains a `gemma_norm` flag) instead of decomposing the norm into fp32 pointwise and reduction kernels. Keep Gemma inputs out of the QuickReduce fused RMSNorm path, which has no weight-bias mode.

On main alone, large prefill does not reach this fallback, so the speedup only shows up together with #57547, which sends prefill above the custom all-reduce pool through it.

---

## Test Plan

- Hardware: 8× MI355X (gfx950)
- Model: `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4`, TP8, `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`
- Base: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-21d93d0d8c0e9627900020382bfce4730e61cab7`, each arm adds only the PRs listed; empty compile caches per run
- Serving A/B: ISL=60000, OSL=600, concurrency `{4, 32, 128}`, range-ratio=1.0
- Accuracy: GPQA diamond, 198 problems, thinking on, temperature=1.0, top-p=0.95, top-k=20, max-tokens=100000, num-threads=32. Same servers as the serving A/B.
- Unit tests:
  - `tests/distributed/test_aiter_rms_fallback.py` — Gemma prefill that misses 1-stage fused AR+RMS goes through regular all-reduce then `fused_add_rms_norm(..., gemma_norm=True)`, and never enters fused QR+RMSNorm
  - `tests/compile/passes/distributed/test_fusion_all_reduce.py` — Gemma variants of the AR+RMS fusion tests; fused graph matches the unfused Gemma residual path

---

## Test Result

### Unit tests

Hardware: 2× MI355X, this PR's diff applied to the nightly above.

```bash
python -m pytest -v --tb=short \
  tests/distributed/test_aiter_rms_fallback.py \
  tests/compile/passes/distributed/test_fusion_all_reduce.py \
  -k "gemma_rmsnorm_falls_back or Gemma"
```

```text
7 passed, 4 skipped
```

### Performance

Median TTFT and output throughput.

#### This PR on main

| Cell | TTFT main | TTFT this PR | Δ | tok/s main | tok/s this PR | Δ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| c=4 | 5954 ms | 5733 ms | −3.7% | 109.5 | 109.4 | −0.1% |
| c=32 | 5513 ms | 5534 ms | +0.4% | 163.4 | 159.4 | −2.5% |
| c=128 | 158478 ms | 158404 ms | 0.0% | 176.1 | 176.0 | −0.1% |

Neutral, as expected: on main the 8k prefill chunks never reach the fallback.

#### With #57547: fallback norm as separate fp32 kernels vs this PR

| Cell | TTFT before | TTFT this PR | Δ | tok/s before | tok/s this PR | Δ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| c=4 | 7035 ms | 5423 ms | **−22.9%** | 95.7 | 113.0 | **+18.1%** |
| c=32 | 6795 ms | 5266 ms | **−22.5%** | 131.8 | 169.1 | **+28.3%** |
| c=128 | 195683 ms | 151098 ms | **−22.8%** | 143.0 | 184.3 | **+28.9%** |

The separate kernels take about 0.75 ms per call against about 0.09 ms for the fused kernel. With 185 calls per 8k prefill chunk, that is about 120 ms of a roughly 550 ms prefill step, which matches the TTFT change.

#### main vs main + #57547 + this PR

| Cell | TTFT main | TTFT both | Δ | tok/s main | tok/s both | Δ |

commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Rust render sends `null` for every unset sampling field and Python `/inference/v1/generate` rejects them. This skips serializing `None` so Rust render output can go straight into Python generate. 

## Claims

- `/v1/chat/completions/render` on the Rust frontend no longer emits `null` in `sampling_params`
- Rust render → Python generate works for requests that leave float fields like `temperature` or `top_p` unset which is nearly every request

## Validation

Before, a minimal chat render returned:

    "sampling_params": {"temperature": null, "top_p": null, "max_tokens": 64, "watermarking": true, ...}

After, the null keys are gone.

Tests added:
- `sampling_params_serialization_omits_unset_fields` (`vllm-text` unit test, includes a round trip)
- `render_chat_omits_unset_sampling_params` (`vllm-server` route test)
- `test_rust_render_sampling_params_without_nulls_validate` (Python test for a body without nulls validates, `"temperature": null` is rejected)

## Details

`vllm_text::SamplingParams` has `Option` fields but no `skip_serializing_none`. The attribute on `GenerateSamplingParams` doesn't reach the flattened inner struct, so the nulls leaked out.

- `watermarking: true` is still emitted. It isn't an `Option` and Python treats `None` and `True` the same
- Nested `structured_outputs` and `repetition_detection` don't emit nulls, so they needed no change
- No schema change. Unset fields come back as `None` through `#[serde(default)]`

No existing PR covers this (checked open PRs for "skip_serializing_none sampling" and "Rust render null sampling_params").

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Core] Check multimodal chunk boundaries before encoder cache reuse
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Apply the existing `disable_chunked_mm_input` boundary guard before warm encoder-cache hits and same-step image deduplication can bypass it. Related to #52306; this addresses a separate cache-hit failure from #52412's equality-boundary fix.

## Claims

- Cached and same-step duplicate images obey the same existing no-chunking guard as uncached images.
- Preserve encoder reuse without changing the guard predicate, EAGLE shift arithmetic, configuration, or public API.
- Add regressions to the existing CPU scheduler suite. No performance improvement is claimed.

## Validation

### Independently rerun CPU checks

On upstream base `e5d33a36e71da9e3e122ac9b139f3ab3b944ef71`, with Python 3.12 and CPU PyTorch 2.13:

```sh
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu VLLM_PLUGINS='' \
uv run --no-project --python .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_encoder_cache_manager.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py -q
```

Result: **241 passed**. The focused command uses `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k test_no_mm_input_chunking -q`: **2 failed, 1 passed** with the original scheduler; **3 passed** with the patch. Original warm-cache scheduling ends at 1024 instead of 400; same-step dedup ends at 1024 instead of 776. These tests run in the existing Buildkite CPU-core step.

Eleven relevant pre-commit hooks, the Python 3.10/3.12 mypy hooks, and `git diff --check` pass on the changed files. The aggregate pre-commit command was attempted but its unrelated actionlint environment could not install because the available Go executable rejects `install`; applicable hooks were run individually.

### Human-submitter GPU validation

The following results come from my GPU validation summary on base `47de9d4d049831914858404c48827837c2d915db`, using the same patch. The assistant reviewed the summary and checked patch correspondence; it did not independently run these GPU tests or inspect their raw logs. After syncing upstream, the encoder-scheduling method, Gemma3 model, Triton backend, and encoder cache manager remain unchanged; GPU tests were not repeated on the newer base.

Environment: WSL2/Ubuntu 24.04, Python 3.12.4, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, RTX 5070 Ti Laptop GPU (12227 MiB). Model: `unsloth/gemma-3-4b-it`, revision `bf46152c47f5dd20b896357cb51abc4c03b8ee8c`, BF16, Triton attention, one request at a time, 512-token scheduling budget. Decoder prefix caching and speculative decoding were disabled; image-content hashing remained enabled.

Eight red/blue-image requests covered cold/warm encoder caches, different text prefixes, and repeated images within one prompt. Traces confirmed actual encoder reuse.

| Check | Original | Patched |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Image splits across eight requests | 4 | 0 |
| First-step end, warm image `[336,596)` | 512 | 336 |
| First-step end, second repeated image `[437,697)` | 512 | 437 |
| Warm-image hidden-state cosine against full-prefill reference | ~0.798–0.799 | ~0.988–0.990 |
| Second repeated-image cosine | ~0.822–0.830 | ~0.980 |

Patched minimum cosine was 0.98610 over the full sequence and 0.98017 over image spans. Seven of eight reported generation comparisons were token-identical; the red cold request differed in punctuation (`Red.` versus `Red`). This is not a claim of universal output identity.

## Details

Both cache fast paths previously returned before the boundary guard. Reusing encoder embeddings does not supply decoder K/V for the image under a different text prefix, so cache state must not bypass the decoder-span policy. The fix relocates the existing guard intact; the shared scheduler path serves both model runners.

Tradeoff: a cached image can now wait for sufficient decoder-token budget. Deferred items are not prematurely pinned; an invalid cached embedding-count mismatch may be reported when the item is admitted instead.

Duplicate checks on 2026-10-02 covered #52306 and its comments, #52412's patch/discussion, and open/merged PRs for the flag and cache/chunking keywords. No existing guard-order fix was found. #52412 changes `<` to `<=`; this PR preserves `<`, and that equality-only change still permits the cache-hit bypass. #59330 changes the P/D prompt-end bound, not these fast paths.

Limits: equality-boundary and prefix-cache mid-item behavior are unchanged. Existing EAGLE rollback arithmetic can still split an adjacent image (for example `[100,300)`, `[300,500)`, shift 1, budget 400 rolls back to 299). This PR does not fix that; GPU validation did not enable EAGLE. HTTP load, production-duration workloads, other attention backends, and quantization were not validated.

commits.pr_title: [Attention] Make the sparse MLA prefill workspace size configurable
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Adds `AttentionConfig.sparse_mla_prefill_workspace_factor`. It replaces the fixed `5 * max_model_len` FlashMLA sparse prefill workspace and the `40 * max_model_len` DSA indexer prefill buffer sized from it. Unset, `VllmConfig` resolves it to 5 up to a 256K `max_model_len` and to 2 above. At a 1M `max_model_len` the fixed reservations hold several GiB per GPU that a long-context deployment can return to the KV cache.

Related: #60874 (right-sizes the DeepSeek-V4.1 copies of these buffers), #42856 (fixed lower factors on SM120 only), #59319 (skips the FlashMLA workspace on the fp8 mixed-batch path).

## Claims

- Up to a 256K `max_model_len` the default keeps every size identical to main.
- Above 256K the default is 2: workspace `2 * max_model_len`, indexer `16 * max_model_len`. `--attention-config.sparse_mla_prefill_workspace_factor=5` restores the main sizes.
- The default resolves once, in `VllmConfig.__post_init__`. KV cache auto-fit can lower `max_model_len` after the workspace is reserved, so a factor derived later could switch from 2 to 5 and size a step past the reservation.
- One knob sizes both buffers. The indexer buffer stays `(576 * 2 // 132) * factor` rows, so it still fits inside the FlashMLA workspace.
- Both chunkers keep each request's context in one gather, so a lower factor changes only how many requests share a gather.
- The floor is 2 (`ge=2`). Under PCP+DCP the per-rank budget is `factor * max_model_len // dcp`, and a full-length request's shard can round up past `max_model_len // dcp`, which `split_prefill_chunks` asserts against.
- GLM-5.3 FP8 on H100 at a 1M `max_model_len` (PCP8, DCP8, TP1): factor 2 raises available KV cache from 9.07 to 18.36 GiB per GPU.

## Validation

**Default, CPU.** On 06a24c32f, a real `VllmConfig` (`Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B`, CPU device) resolves the factor and both buffer sizes as follows:

| `max_model_len` | factor | workspace | indexer |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 163840 | 5 | 5x | 40x |
| 262144 | 5 | 5x | 40x |
| 262145 | 2 | 2x | 16x |
| 1048576 | 2 | 2x | 16x |

An explicit factor of 3 at 1M is kept, and `AttentionConfig(sparse_mla_prefill_workspace_factor=1)` raises a validation error. `test_indexer_prefill_budget_matches_compressed_workspace` reads the resolved factor through `create_vllm_config`; it needs a GPU, so CI runs it in the `v1/attention` job. pre-commit (ruff, mypy, `validate-config`, test tethering) passes on the changed files.

**GLM-5.3 on H100, same sizes.** We run GLM-5.3 FP8 in production with these exact sizes (workspace 2x, indexer 16x) applied to the same two functions on our vLLM build. The prefill engines are PCP8, DCP8, TP1, `--max-model-len 1048576`, `fp8_ds_mla`, block size 64, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.93`.

| | factor 5 | factor 2 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Available KV cache per GPU | 9.07 GiB | 18.36 GiB |
| KV cache tokens per 8-GPU engine | 1.40M to 1.42M | 2.63M to 2.88M |
| 1M-token code-recall prompt | passes, 120.5 to 122.0 s | passes, 122.6 s |

All 28 production prefill engines have run factor 2 since 2026-10-10 18:08 UTC, and every one booted without OOM.

**This branch on GPU: not run.** The production numbers come from the same sizes on our build.

## Details

- **Why a config field.** The neighbouring sparse-MLA and indexer knobs (`sparse_mla_force_mqa`, `indexer_kv_dtype`, `hisparse_config`) live in `AttentionConfig`. `get_prefill_workspace_size` now takes the `VllmConfig`, like `get_max_prefill_buffer_size` already does.
- **Scope.** The FlashMLA workspace part applies to `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` with a quantized DS-MLA cache. `get_max_prefill_buffer_size` also sizes the indexer in `deepseek_v2` (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.x), `deepseek_v32`, `deepseek_v4`, `deepseek_v41`, `hy_v4` and `glm5next`, so the factor applies there too. The DeepSeek-V4.1 FlashMLA workspace is sized in `models/deepseek_v41` and does not read it.
- **Cost.** A step gathers in more passes only when its prefill requests hold more than `factor * max_model_len` context tokens in total. At the default above 256K (factor 2), that takes three or more concurrent near-full-length prefills.
- **Not a duplicate.** Open PRs found with `gh pr list --state open --search` for "sparse prefill workspace", "prefill workspace size configurable", "flashmla sparse workspace", "indexer prefill buffer" and "workspace factor":
  - #42856 lowers the factors to 2 and 8 on SM120 only, stacked on #41834.
  - #60874 changes only the DeepSeek-V4.1 builders.
  - #59319 drops the reservation on the mixed-batch path. On the separate prefill path this knob still sizes it, and the two PRs touch one shared call line in `FlashMLASparseImpl.__init__`.
  - None makes the size configurable.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][weight loader] Stop warning when a parameter only widens the weight
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Follow-up to [#51792](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51792), which added this warning. `AutoWeightsLoader` emits it whenever a checkpoint weight's dtype differs from the parameter it lands in. A parameter declared wider than the checkpoint is a deliberate choice and the copy is exact, so that line reports nothing and buries the narrowing cases it was added for. Log the float widenings that cannot change a value at DEBUG instead of WARNING; every other mismatch still warns exactly as before.

## Claims

- A 48-layer Qwen3.x emits this warning 36 times at every start, once per linear-attention layer, for fp32 decay accumulators reading a bf16 `A_log` — counted from 180 occurrences over 5 starts in a serving log. All 36 are exact widenings, so the change is expected to log them at DEBUG instead; the post-change count was not measured on a model run.
- No other warning changes: the condition only subtracts from the cases that already fired.
- The conversions moved to DEBUG are exact for every finite input, not approximately: all 63,488 finite fp16 and 65,280 finite bf16 bit patterns round-trip through fp32 and fp64 unchanged, and fp32 round-trips through fp64.
- Nothing about loading changes — same values, same returned names. Only the level of the line changes; it is still logged, at DEBUG.
- Every other dtype mismatch still warns, including the fp8 pairs whose range looks wider but whose subnormals are shorter.

## Validation

On the branch point (`92044241a0`) and this PR, on CPU: load one parameter through `AutoWeightsLoader` for each stored → declared pair and record the level of the `Attempted to load weight` line.

| stored → declared | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bfloat16 → float32`, `float16 → float32`, `float32 → float64` | WARNING | DEBUG |
| `float32 → bfloat16`, `float16 → bfloat16` | WARNING | WARNING |
| `float8_e4m3fnuz → float8_e4m3fn` | WARNING | WARNING |

`pytest tests/models/test_utils.py`: 9 passed, the same tests as the branch point.

Exhaustive check of the pairs moved to DEBUG, run outside the suite: every finite fp16 and bf16 bit pattern cast to fp32 and to fp64 and back compares bit-identical, and none of them loses a value at `tiny/4`, `±max`, `1e-30` or `0.1`. Across the 8 float dtypes checked, 56 ordered pairs, the 5 widenings moved to DEBUG lose nothing at the probed values.

No model run, no multi-GPU, no performance measurement.

## Details

**Why a whitelist and not a predicate.** Comparing what the two formats hold reads as the general answer and is not. `eps`, `max` and `min` describe the normal range, so they miss the subnormal reach: `float8_e4m3fnuz` has the same 3 mantissa bits and a smaller `max` than `float8_e4m3fn`, which makes it look strictly narrower, but its exponent bias is one higher, 8 against 7, so its smallest subnormal is 2⁻¹⁰ against 2⁻⁹ and `0.0009765625` loads as `0.0`. A predicate built on those three fields calls that cast lossless and demotes a warning that matters. `torch.finfo` exposes no subnormal bound to repair it with, and the existing `is_lossless_cast()` in `vllm/utils/torch_utils.py` compares `resolution`, `min` and `max`, and returns `True` for this very pair, so reusing it would carry the same gap. Listing the widenings that are exact by construction — fp16, bf16 or fp32 into fp32 or fp64 — is smaller and easier to verify at this scope.

**Relation to existing work.** [#51836](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51836) proposes config-driven changes to Qwen parameter dtypes, which is separate work on the parameters themselves; it is not landed, and it would need a config field present in each affected checkpoint. This PR changes the log level only: known-lossless widenings log at DEBUG instead of WARNING, every other dtype mismatch still warns, and no parameter or loaded value moves.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][MLA] Cut ~21x host dispatch from the MLA metadata build
commits.pr_body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Scope: this is a host-dispatch microbenchmark, not an end-to-end throughput claim.**
> The numbers below are measured on the host build path, with per-call dispatch counts. Against a multi-millisecond decode step a
> change of this size sits inside run-to-run variation (~1% on a conc=1 arm), so
> **no measurable serving throughput improvement is claimed, and none should be
> inferred.** The value is removing host torch dispatches that serialize against the GPU on a path that is
> on the critical path at low concurrency. Details under "End-to-end (side note)".

## Summary

Two spots on the MLA attention metadata build spend more time in PyTorch
dispatch than in the work they do. Both operate on tensors that are already
host-side and hold one entry per request, and both run on **every** build,
between decode steps.

### 1. `AiterMLAMetadataBuilder._uniform_padded_mtp_qo_len`

Eight tensor dispatches — `sum()/item()`, a boolean-mask index, `numel()`,
`torch.all`, `eq`, `torch.nonzero`, `item()`, `torch.any` — to decide a single
integer. `qo_len` is derived from `query_start_loc_cpu`.

### 2. `MLACommonMetadataBuilder.build`, non-causal multi-token decode

A validation block using `torch.count_nonzero`, two `torch.all` calls and two
tensor-to-bool conversions (each lowering to `aten::is_nonzero`), purely to
raise a `ValueError` on a malformed query block.

Both now read the tensor out once and decide on Python ints.

## Results

Host cost, measured **without a GPU**. Both inputs are CPU tensors, so there is
no device work and no profiler involved in these numbers.

**`_uniform_padded_mtp_qo_len`**

| reqs | before | after | speedup | saved |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1.88 µs | 0.32 µs | **5.9×** | 1.56 µs |
| 2 | 17.62 µs | 0.53 µs | **33.6×** | 17.10 µs |
| 8 | 17.65 µs | 0.71 µs | **24.8×** | 16.94 µs |

**non-causal query-block validation**

| reqs | before | after | speedup | saved |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 11.88 µs | 0.84 µs | **14.1×** | 11.04 µs |
| 2 | 12.44 µs | 0.89 µs | **13.9×** | 11.55 µs |
| 8 | 12.58 µs | 1.20 µs | **10.5×** | 11.38 µs |

Combined at 2 requests: **30.06 µs → 1.42 µs, ~21×, 14 tensor dispatches
removed per build.**

The step from one request to two in the first table is the padded-CUDA-graph
case: with dummy rows present the function stops early-returning and runs the
full `nonzero`/`any` path, which is the shape a graph-captured decode hits.

## Why this path matters

On a Kimi-K3 conc=1 384K-context decode trace, all 8 GPUs are idle across the
metadata-build window between decode steps, so host time there is on the
critical path rather than overlapped. These two sites account for the
`count_nonzero`, `is_nonzero` and `eq`/`nonzero` operations visible in that
window.

## Correctness

No FLOPs change and no device work changes; both sites return small integers
and booleans.

- `_uniform_padded_mtp_qo_len`: **34067 cases, 0 mismatches** — exhaustive over
  every `qo_len` combination up to 4 requests × length 4 crossed with every
  plausible `num_decode_tokens`, plus 20000 randomised larger cases. Covers
  empty, all-zero, zero-interior, non-divisible totals, `uniform_qo_len <= 1`
  and trailing-zero inputs.
- non-causal validation: **21364 cases, 0 mismatches** — exhaustive over every
  query-length combination up to 5 requests × length 3, plus 20000 randomised
  cases, comparing all three returned predicates.

The `ValueError` text is unchanged: it now formats a list rather than calling
`.tolist()` on a tensor.

## Tests run

```
ruff check vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py \
           vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py
All checks passed!

ruff format --check <same two files>
2 files already formatted
```

Equivalence harnesses were run inside `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm` on CPU; output is
the case counts quoted above.

## Not a duplicate

Searched open PRs before writing this:

```
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "_uniform_padded_mtp_qo_len"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "rocm_aiter_mla host"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "non-causal MLA uniform query block"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "mla_attention count_nonzero"
```

Nearby open PRs (#57085, #57464, #54546, #58344) touch this area but none
addresses the host cost of these two functions.

## End-to-end (side note)

Deliberately last, and not the claim being made. End-to-end effect at this
operating point depends on how many metadata builds occur per step and on the
tuning of surrounding kernels, which is out of scope here. On our conc=1
Kimi-K3 configuration the expected effect is well under the run-to-run spread
we measure (~0.8%), so the function-level speedup above is the honest result.

---

run by the submitter on MI355X hardware, and every changed line was reviewed by
the submitter.

<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Remove cascade attention from vLLM: its kernels, heuristics, metadata, scheduler/KV-cache plumbing, model-runner logic, config/flag handling, tests, and docs.

Cascade attention has been opt-in (`disable_cascade_attn=True` by default), already hard-disabled for FlashInfer (see #25679), force-disabled for async spec decode / DBO / batch invariance / CPU, and unsupported by most backends — yet it still costs a per-step scheduler scan, branches in the model runner and backends, and recurring bugs (#55674, #47183, #39208, #55227, #53690 are open fixes/workarounds that this PR makes moot).

**This PR is non-breaking for hardware plugins.** Plugin-facing APIs (`build(common_prefix_len, ...)`, `SchedulerOutput.num_common_prefix_blocks`, etc.) are kept as deprecated no-ops; a follow-up PR removes them once plugin maintainers have been notified.

## Claims

- No behavior change for default configurations (cascade was off by default); net **-901 lines in `vllm/`** (+504 / -1,405; most `+` lines are de-indentation in the FA/AITER forward paths after removing the cascade branch).
- The scheduler no longer scans the running request's blocks every step.
- Out-of-tree plugins keep working unchanged (checked against vllm-ascend, tpu-inference, vllm-gaudi, vllm-spyre, vllm-metal).
- `--disable-cascade-attn` / `disable_cascade_attn=` still parse; they warn and have no effect (to be removed in v0.33.0, same schedule as `--log-config-file`).
